question: Has the Stellar mainnet ever halted? What happened, and how was it resolved?

golden.answer: Yes. On May 15, 2019 the network stopped closing ledgers for about an hour because too many validators were offline to reach consensus. Nothing forked and no funds were lost; validators restarted it by coordinating a quorum-set change. On April 6, 2021 SDF's validators and Horizon stalled, but the network kept closing ledgers; the Protocol 16 upgrade fixed that bug.
keyFacts: Stellar mainnet halted on May 15, 2019 when validators could not reach consensus.
The 2019 halt caused no fork and no loss of funds.
Validators ended the 2019 halt by coordinating a quorum-set change.
In April 2021 SDF's validators stalled but the network kept closing ledgers.
avoid: Do NOT claim the Stellar mainnet has never halted.
Do NOT describe the April 2021 SDF validator outage as a network-wide halt.
golden.notes: SDF reports 67 minutes for the 2019 halt; press reported about two hours. Accept either.

During the entirety of the SDF node downtime, the Stellar network remained online. ... The network itself did not halt.
On April 10, 2021, Stellar network validators voted to upgrade the network to Protocol 16, which contains a fix
Certain validators dropped off the network ... The SDF horizon cluster and validators are back up. Posted Apr 06, 2021 - 19:00 UTC

Stellar's blockchain suffered a 'cascading failure' that halted transactions for roughly two hours on May 15.

corroboration.claim: The Stellar public network stopped closing ledgers on May 15, 2019 because it could not reach consensus.

evidence.note: 'During that time no ledgers were closed and no transactions were processed.' Keybase took a validator down for maintenance while others were shaky or down.
2019-05-16 report of the May 15 transaction freeze.
SDF post-mortem: halted 1:14pm PT, ledgers resumed 2:21pm PT, 67 minutes.
'roughly two hours'. The golden does not pin a duration.
Research run found no source that reconciles the figures; it infers that press counted through a later brief stoppage. Left disputed.

corroboration.claim: SDF's FAQ says the network has halted once, for 67 minutes on May 15, 2019; the 2019 post-mortem also records a brief second stoppage that day.

evidence.note: 'In the history of Stellar, the network has only halted once-for 67 minutes on May 15, 2019.'
UPDATE: 'The network was taken down briefly while we repaired this.' The golden names the May 15, 2019 halt and does not count halts.
Research run found no other full mainnet halt through 2026 and quotes the same FAQ line.

corroboration.claim: The 2019 halt caused no fork and no loss of funds, and ended when key validators coordinated a quorum-set change.

evidence.note: 'No one lost their money; no one's balances were confused by a fork.' 'key validators on the network coordinated a configuration change in which quourumsets were reduced'.
'no transactions were validated until developers resolved the issue'.

corroboration.claim: On April 6, 2021 SDF's validators and public Horizon stopped while the network kept processing transactions; Protocol 16 (voted April 10, 2021) fixed the bug.

evidence.note: SDF nodes stopped around 1:00 am PDT and were back at 11:28 am PDT; 'The network itself did not halt.'
Incident 'Certain validators dropped off the network', resolved 2021-04-06 19:00 UTC.
Protocol 16 'contains a fix that resolves the issue that caused several nodes to go offline'.

truth.notes: The 2019 post-mortem's update records a brief second stoppage while quorum sets were repaired, so the golden does not say the network halted only once. Sibling check: q-protocol-24-whisk-incident covers the October 2025 state-archival bug, which was not a halt.
